request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The audit now gets the new ROLLUP and TOTALS lines, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works.** The people's claimed and due-total figures were only worked out in the browser, so I added `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/RollupService.java` to work them out on the server the same way. Every change takes a snapshot of the figures before it runs. After its own audit line it compares the figures again and writes:
- one `ROLLUP` line for each person whose claimed or due-total moved, in the order people were added (a newly added person always counts as moved);
- then one `TOTALS` line if the sheet's claimed-total or due-total moved.

These lines are written only when the change commits, so a refused change still writes nothing. A change that moves no figure writes no extra lines, which covers setting a rate to the value it already has and settling at the current figure.

**Where it's hooked in:** adding and editing a person; adding, editing, opening, settling and voiding a claim; setting a rate; taking a statement; and changing the sheet's today. Changing today has no audit line of its own, so the server now passes the user's name through to record `by=`.

**Two things that differ from what you might expect:**
- **Line format:** the request says `ROLLUP name=<name>`, but the test expects `person=<name>` (like the claim lines), so I followed the test.
- **Statements:** a statement can move a figure. If a grade has no rate for today, the person's due-total shows n/a until a statement fixes their claims' dues, and then it shows a number. Following "every change", a statement is followed by ROLLUP lines when that happens. None of the test's statements move a figure, so this case isn't exercised.
